purpose: Small golden dataset for judging the quality of Dutch word explanations. These cases define what a good answer should get right without requiring one exact wording.

cases.risk: A model may incorrectly infer separability from the spelling and teach a false conjugation pattern.
reference_facts: the finite form stays together, for example: ik vervang de lamp
the past participle is vervangen, for example: ik heb de lamp vervangen
the verb does not split as ik vang ... ver
critical_failures: recommends a split form such as ik vang ... ver
recommends an incorrect past participle formed by adding ge- to vervangen
quality_criteria: explains the useful conjugation consequence clearly
keeps the explanation understandable for an A2-B1 learner

cases.risk: A model may treat bezighouden like an inseparable be- verb even though bezig is the separable particle here.
reference_facts: a common reflexive construction is zich bezighouden met
a correct present-tense example is: ik houd me bezig met Nederlands
a correct perfect example is: ik heb me met Nederlands beziggehouden
critical_failures: recommends keeping bezighouden together in a finite main-clause form where it should split
gives a past participle that omits the correct beziggehouden form
quality_criteria: shows the separation in a useful sentence rather than only naming the grammar rule
handles the reflexive pronoun naturally when using zich bezighouden met

cases.risk: A model may reduce gezellig to one English gloss such as cozy and miss how broadly it is used in Dutch.
reference_facts: gezellig is context-dependent and can describe a pleasant, sociable or cozy atmosphere, activity, place or company
there is no single English translation that fits every use
critical_failures: presents gezellig as having one fixed English meaning in every context
gives Dutch examples that are grammatically wrong or clearly unnatural
quality_criteria: uses examples that demonstrate at least two natural contexts when possible
explains the idea more helpfully than a bare dictionary translation
keeps examples conversational and suitable for an A2-B1 learner

cases.risk: A model may give a technically possible translation without teaching the common everyday constructions learners actually need.
reference_facts: afspraak commonly refers to an appointment or an agreement/arrangement depending on context
een afspraak maken is a common construction
een afspraak hebben bij de huisarts is a natural everyday use
critical_failures: gives a materially wrong core meaning
teaches an unidiomatic construction as the normal way to make or have an appointment
quality_criteria: includes at least one common collocation or construction
makes the context-dependent meaning clear without overcomplicating it
